Subject: Transportation Plan to Reduce Costs and Protect Service Levels
Date: [Insert Date]

Situation:
We operate a broad network of warehouses and factories supplying stores, customers, and regional hubs. Transportation spend is a major cost driver, and our service commitments depend on placing inventory in the right locations on time. A clear, data-driven shipping plan will help us control costs while meeting customer expectations.

Problem:
We need to decide how much to ship from each source to each destination, recognizing that:
- Each source has limited available inventory and operational capacity.
- Each destination has a required quantity that must be met in full.
- Shipping costs vary by route based on distance, mode, and carrier rates.
- Shipments must be in whole unit quantities; no partial loads are allowed.

Our goal is to cover every destination’s requirement without exceeding any source’s available inventory, using the least-cost mix of routes. Achieving this will reduce total transportation spend, minimize the need for expedites, and maintain high on-time performance.

Plan:
Using the attached data set, we will align available inventory with destination needs and route costs to develop a practical shipment allocation by lane. We will prioritize economical lanes, respect source and destination limits, and ensure all moves are planned in whole units. The deliverable will be a recommended shipping plan that meets all requirements at the lowest achievable total cost, along with key trade-offs to inform final approvals.
